THE MOVEMENT

CSDA+ for the creative tech with a heart for creatives.

Our Mission

Art Nexus is a dedicated showcase and seller platform empowering local creators to display their work, share their visual narratives, and thrive in an independent creative marketplace. We bridge the gap between passion and sustainability, giving artists a direct platform to connect with collectors.

Our Roots & Legacy

Beyond a marketplace, a community is born here. Art Nexus is built around the Cordillera School of Digital Arts’s (CSDA) 20 years of excellence and its foundational Artrovert community. For two decades, this movement has gathered, celebrated, and embraced the unique local creative culture, while actively protecting and nurturing budding artists.

Local preview storage

Artwork releases and previews, visibility metadata, video URLs and available YouTube/Vimeo thumbnail links, and Creator social links are saved in this browser’s app storage. Artwork is resized here to a 720p WebP preview (up to 1280 × 720 landscape or 720 × 1280 portrait, no larger than 300,000 bytes); the original file is not uploaded. Public profile/Browse listings work only inside this local preview. Share URLs, Drive/IPFS/Arweave resolution, cloud media sync, and production catalog sync are not connected. Optional master-pointer metadata remains local, is syntax-checked only, and is never resolved or fetched. Removing an item removes its app copy, but is not a promise of forensic deletion from browser or device backups.

Cooperative governance · not implemented

This prototype has no member registry, eligibility rules, voting, elections, appeals, or dispute process. It does not claim that a legal cooperative exists or that members have one-member-one-vote rights.

Campaigns & contact consent · disabled

This preview does not collect campaign subscribers or send campaigns. Double opt-in, separate contact storage, export, and purge/deletion workflows are not implemented. Commission proposal previews are separate local records and are not delivered to an artist.

Prototype data notice · not a legal privacy policy

Creator release metadata and 720p WebP previews, video and social-link URLs, private WIP notes and previews, artist-managed transaction links, local commission proposals, bookmark collections, and device-local heart selections are stored in this browser’s app storage. On a configured signed-in Creator account, private local studio data is kept in browser storage scoped to that account on this device; it is not included in account-state sync. Local profile data may also be saved here, and browser/device backups may retain copies. Hearts are not sent to an Art Nexus server, do not produce public/shared counts, and do not notify an artist. Follow/follower counts are not recorded. Account/profile requests may use configured service routes; server-side logs, retention, and operator access require separate verification. This prototype notice is not a legal policy, does not state legal compliance, and does not guarantee permanent or forensic erasure.

Private Google Drive Storage

Keep original artwork in your Google My Drive vault. Art Nexus caches only a small WebP Browse thumbnail; controlled previews and paid downloads are served through the app.

Checking secure Drive connection…

Creator Storage Agreement

Review this agreement before connecting Google Drive. Your Drive originals remain private; Art Nexus will not make them public or grant “anyone with the link” access.

  1. Permission scope. You authorize Art Nexus to use Google’s drive.file permission for files the app creates or handles. The app creates a folder named My Drive/ArtNexus_Vault for its uploads and does not request broad access to your Drive.
  2. Originals stay yours and private. Raw artwork originals and derived zoom previews upload directly from your browser to Google Drive. Art Nexus stores encrypted OAuth refresh tokens and file references on its server; it does not change Drive sharing permissions. Disconnecting removes Art Nexus’s stored connection but leaves your files in Drive.
  3. Browse preview. Art Nexus generates a 720p WebP preview in your browser, limited to 1280 × 720 landscape or 720 × 1280 portrait and no larger than 300,000 bytes, for the public Browse feed. This preview is stored in the configured Art Nexus cache; that is nonzero storage, separate from your private master.
  4. Controlled access. Visitors can request only a derived preview through Art Nexus, not the Drive master. A downloadable master is released only after the server verifies a paid order, using a short-lived one-time link. No payment claim is accepted from a browser redirect alone.
  5. Keep files available. Do not move to trash, delete, or remove the app’s access to source files while a listing is public. If the source or preview returns 403/404, Art Nexus will hide/unlist that work. Reconnect or re-upload to restore availability; payment delivery cannot work while the source is inaccessible.
  6. Account and provider requirements. Google OAuth, Drive, Supabase cache, and payment delivery work only when this deployment is configured and verified. Google may apply its own quotas and policies. Never share your OAuth credentials or private Drive links with buyers.

No email is required to read or accept this agreement. Connecting Google Drive later requires a signed-in Creator account with a verified email, plus configured Google OAuth.

Masters and derived 720p WebP previews stay private in your Google Drive. Only the bounded 720p WebP Browse preview is publicly cached. Local-preview mode continues to work without a Drive connection.

New releases publish publicly. This browser preview adds them to your Creator profile and Browse. Existing private drafts remain private and are never published automatically. Nothing is synced to a production catalog.

Artwork files may be JPEG, PNG, WebP, or GIF up to 15 MB. A 720p WebP preview must fit within 1280 × 720 landscape or 720 × 1280 portrait and the strict 300,000-byte ceiling; saving fails visibly if it does not. The original is not sent by this local-preview flow. Video releases save an HTTPS link and, when available, a YouTube/Vimeo thumbnail link. Vimeo may use public oEmbed metadata; showing thumbnails may contact the provider. The in-app player loads only after a visitor clicks Play, and the video itself is not uploaded. Local release data stays in this browser; removing an item removes its app copy, but browser/device backups may retain data.
